recommendations.rationale: Deferred, not executed in this phase: at the saved projected state of update 34 (t = 0.35 s, where the recorded applied tensions leave tendon 5 at 0.0 N), compare the recorded input with an instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed 0.01 s horizon to quantify local endpoint speed/position differences. This measures only local braking authority at one projected state; it cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or controller/backend mismatch when these predict the same endpoint, and it cannot identify the dominant settling cause.

Deferred, not executed in this phase: at one saved projected state whose effective horizon matches the authorized 0.01 s horizon, change only terminal_tip_speed_weight (displayed as 0) to a nonzero value and compare the two local controller solves; this isolates the local plan/endpoint effect of the tip-speed objective term. It measures local plan and endpoint differences only and does not establish closed-loop settling or causation, nor does it prove cost-term importance for the shipped configuration.

Deferred: before any numerical check or parameter discussion, read the retained per-update optimization_raw_status, optimization_selected_iteration and actual_tension_n for updates 0..34 (source.solver_status, source.plan_selection, source.applied_tensions) to verify the User_Requested_Stop / early-stop pattern and the tendon-5 saturation claim update-by-update. This is evidence reading only; it executes no control change and cannot by itself attribute the settling failure.

Deferred: if the single authorized 0.01 s bounded check cannot discriminate among the candidate explanations, or if its result depends on extrapolation to the 0.05 s settling window, report the settling cause as inconclusive rather than advancing a dominant root cause; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot account for an entire settling failure and no closed-loop replay capability is retained.

attribution.reason: 34 of 35 updates ended in User_Requested_Stop with 35 deadline misses and a mean update time of 17.075 s against a 0.01 s control period (fact_scheduling_stop_counts), which is consistent with most accepted plans coming from early-stop / feasible-suboptimal returns rather than converged solves. The retained per-update optimization_raw_status, optimization_selected_iteration and actual_tension_n were not read this phase, so this pattern is not verified update-by-update and its contribution to the terminal 0.635 m/s tip speed is not established.

The displayed configuration sets holding_brake_lead_s = 0, holding_tip_speed_weight = 0 and terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0 (fact_controller_config), i.e. no explicit tip-speed penalty term, which is a plausible contributor to a residual terminal speed of 0.635 m/s. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions and scaling, and no bounded saved-state check was executed in this phase, so the effect remains a hypothesis.

regenerate_warm_states = true with numerical_source = 'bundled_guess' is displayed (fact_controller_config), but control_snapshots.json (full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces) is not retained and no bounded local check was executed, so no retained signal links warm-start regeneration to the residual late-window speed or position error.

In the retained one-step prediction at update 34 no tendon reaches the 8.0 N limit and tendon 5 is at 0.0 N (fact_terminal_update_tensions), so saturation is not displayed in that channel; the parallel retained actual_tension_n channel and the remaining updates were not read this phase, so the saturation claim is neither confirmed nor ruled out.

The configured horizon is 10 (fact_controller_config) while per-update effective_horizon is only carried in artifact 8665c9eb0ebe506e281863969240de828087ac8c214265363a536c530c8d500a, which the request scope states is retained but not accessible via evidence.read; the effective horizon per update therefore could not be compared with the configured horizon.

The one-step predictions are projected-model (implicit Euler, 1 substep, 0.01 s control period) statements about the next execution timestamp, and backend tip motion exists only as a retained-but-unreadable artifact; no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution tool is exposed, and a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot account for an entire 50 ms settling window.

The host-supplied scheduling statement for this run specifies synchronous controller calls completing before fixed-count backend steps and that wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so the measured late-window speed and position error reflect the simulated closed loop rather than a wall-clock overrun artifact.

facts.statement: Reach tolerance was met (reach_passed = true, terminal_error_m = 0.00764 m <= 0.01 m) while the sampled settling criterion failed (sampled_settling_passed = false): late-window maximum tip speed 1.581 m/s against the 0.02 m/s limit and late-window maximum position error 0.0581 m against the 0.01 m position limit over the 0.05 s window; the terminal sample still shows tip speed 0.635 m/s.

The run ended 34 of 35 controller updates with User_Requested_Stop and 1 with Solve_Succeeded, recorded 35 deadline misses, and averaged 17.075 s of update computation against a 0.01 s control period (29 initialization-selected, 6 non-initialization-selected updates).

The displayed controller parameters set horizon 10, holding_brake_lead_s 0, holding_tip_speed_weight 0, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0 (terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001), regenerate_warm_states true and numerical_source 'bundled_guess'.

At the last retained one-step prediction (update 34, t = 0.35 s) applied_tension_n = [3.1759, 2.7574, 1.42e-08, 0.8930, 0.1273, 0.0] N with tendon 5 at 0.0 N; every listed value is below the 8.0 N per-tendon force limit, so force-limit saturation is not displayed in this retained channel.

gates.reason: Terminal position error is within the 0.01 m reach tolerance.
Late-window maximum tip speed exceeds the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.
Late-window maximum position error exceeds the 0.01 m settling position limit.

limitations: No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution tool is available; full trajectories are not present in every request, and the existing numerical checks use a projected GVS state and a bounded 0.01 s horizon rather than a full backend replay.

No saved-state numerical check was executed in this initial phase (prediction_braking and local_comparison were deferred); a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot explain an entire 0.05 s settling failure, so no dominance claim is made.

recommended_actions: Defer the single authorized prediction_braking probe to the next phase: at the saved projected state of update 34 (t = 0.35 s), compare the recorded input with an instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed 0.01 s horizon to quantify local endpoint speed/position differences.

Defer the single authorized local_comparison to the next phase: change exactly one weight at a saved state, e.g. terminal_tip_speed_weight from 0 to nonzero (or holding_tip_speed_weight), to observe whether the local plan and endpoint move; requires a saved effective horizon matching the authorized horizon.

Before any parameter change, read the retained per-update optimization_raw_status, optimization_selected_iteration and actual_tension_n (updates 0..34) to verify the User_Requested_Stop / early-stop pattern and the tendon-5 saturation claim update-by-update.
Treat a 0.01 s probe as non-explanatory for the 0.05 s settling window: if the bounded checks cannot discriminate candidates, report the settling cause as inconclusive rather than extrapolating.
